Hi Asha — thanks for sending this over and great to hear the team is ready. Short answers up-front, followed by examples below.

1) Token accounting: we meter request tokens (prompt + metadata) and response tokens (generation). Billing is per-token aggregated across the invoice period; prompt + completion are additive on the same call.

2) Context handling: we support both per-call accounting and conversation-level amortization. For a single 12k prompt into a 16k model the full 12k is billed as request tokens; if you then request a short completion (200 tokens), we'll bill 12,200 tokens for that call. For conversation mode with persistent KV cache, repeated prefixes can be credited under our "prefix reuse" rule (see examples).

3) Rounding/minimums: the default quantum is 16 tokens for hosted API (i.e., we round up usage per-call to the nearest 16-token bucket). For Dedicated or Private pilots we can adjust the quantum — Marissa is CC'd and can detail waiver options.

Attached is a short one-pager (pilot-MAP.pdf) and I've asked Marissa for sample invoice lines. Ben will add a few operational notes on streaming vs one-shot.

Hi Asha — Marissa from Billing here. Below are concrete billable examples and the pilot concession options. Reposting Grace's summary for context.

Billing examples (hosted API, default quantum = 16 tokens):
- Example A (large call): prompt 12,000 tokens + completion 1,000 tokens = 13,000 tokens. Rounding: 13,000 rounded up to nearest 16 -> 13,008 billable tokens.
- Example B (small call): prompt 200 tokens + completion 50 tokens = 250 tokens -> rounded up to 256 tokens.
- Example C (streaming partials): for streaming we bill the final committed tokens per call; intermediate partials are not billed until the stream completes. If you use heartbeat keepalive without sending extra tokens, no additional token charge applies.

Conversation amortization (prefix reuse):
- If you reuse a 2k-token system prompt across 100 calls within the same conversation window, we apply an amortization credit so you aren't billed full 2k every time. The amortization window is configurable; default is 24 hours for hosted pilots.

Minimums & waivers:
- Standard: monthly invoice with no per-call minimum, but we do enforce the 16-token quantum per-call.
- Pilot concession: we can waive the 16-token quantum for the first 2 months for a pilot under $10k/mo committed usage (i.e., we'll bill exact tokens without rounding for the pilot).
- For Dedicated pilots we can set a smaller quantum (e.g., 4 tokens) — requires capacity booking.

Attached is a sample invoice extract for a high-volume day and a low-volume sample (sample-invoice.csv). If you want the math in a spreadsheet, I can push a detailed workbook.

Let me know if the two-month quantum waiver works for procurement; if yes, I'll document it in the SOW.

Quick operational notes from engineering/sales-eng:

- Streaming vs one-shot: streaming doesn't change billing semantics — final token count wins. However, streaming can reduce perceived latency and avoid re-sending large prefixes if you keep a session-level KV cache. If you do aggressive micro-streaming (many tiny commits) the per-call quantum can cause overhead; for that pattern we recommend batching on the client or enabling our session aggregation feature.

- Long prompts near model context limit: if a client sends a 16k prompt and also requests a 2k completion, some model variants will reject the call; Redwood will return the error and no completion tokens are billed (you only pay for the request tokens). We instrument these rejects separately in the invoice (error_code column).

- Sample playbook (short):
  * One-shot high-volume: use per-call accounting, accept default quantum; optimize prompts for shorter completions.
  * Conversation-heavy: enable prefix reuse + 24h window; ask for amortization credit in pilot SOW.

I'll volunteer to run a quick cost run if you share the CSV Grace requested. Happy to hop on a 30-min technical Q&A with your platform team.
